summary.headline: Expleo Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 2,863 million, but constant-currency growth was only 0.7%.
summary.overview: Reported operating revenue grew 11.9% YoY and 2.5% QoQ to INR 2,863 million, helped mainly by Rupee depreciation against the Euro and US dollar. At constant currency, revenue grew just 0.7% YoY and fell 0.9% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 15.5% versus 15.6% a year ago and 16.6% in Q3, reflecting wage increments partly offset by efficiency gains. Management guided to sustainable double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margins held near current levels for FY27, while flagging AI-driven pricing pressure on existing accounts.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Management said Europe is the fastest-growing region and is leading growth, with significant work flowing in; Q4 on-site revenue growth came from Europe BFSI.

segments.name: BFSI (technology)
segments.commentary: Management said BFSI performed extremely well and is the bulk of the technology business; no financial services proposal is going out without an AI element.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (engineering)
segments.commentary: Management said aero/defence performed very well; it is about 11% of total revenue per an analyst, and margins are in line with the overall company. Israel and Make in India test-bench demand were cited.

segments.name: Group (related party)
segments.commentary: Revenue from the Expleo Group is about 30% of total revenue per management, with a 32-33% share cited in answer to a question; the share rose by 2-3 basis points.

guidance_outlook: Direction is sustainable double-digit revenue growth in FY27, per CEO, with the caveat that predictions are hard given uncertainties.
EBITDA to remain at current levels; CEO reiterated the 15-16% range without other income when asked, and said he is confident in that range.
FY27 strategy has four levers: new logo acquisition, growing top-20 accounts on expleo.ai, sector focus on payments and aerospace/defence, and people.
Partner-led growth with more than 15 partners identified for joint go-to-market; benefits expected in upcoming quarters.

M&A: about 9 assets identified in the last 3 months, 3 in due diligence, and management said a closing is very likely in the upcoming quarter. Target focus is the US, with AI, data or Salesforce capabilities.
Dividend deferred to prioritise M&A execution, per Chairman.
capex_capacity: New Bangalore facility inaugurated on the call, about 4x larger lab for test bench manufacturing and assembly, plus larger technology team space.
Management has invested in payment simulators compatible with Mastercard, Visa, RuPay, American Express and UPI, ahead of 2028 regulatory deadlines; significant spend expected in CY26 and CY27.
Egypt (Cairo) chosen as the strategic new-country market for FY27; no revenue target given.
INR 100 crore loans given to Expleo Group entities as related-party transactions at arm's length, earning about 9.5% to 10%.
Attrition moderated at around 15%; 70% of the organisation is now AI qualified, with a target of 95% to 100% by around September or October 2026.
demand_pricing: Ticket sizes are shrinking as AI shortens engagements; the same work is now expected at 40% to 50% of prior effort, per CEO.

AI productivity gains range from 20% to 60% by service (code generation up to 60%, automated test execution 30% to 40%); most savings are passed to customers, with premium pricing on AI services not offsetting that.
Win rates on renewals were described as not a challenge, with critical clients often with Expleo for 20 to 25 years; the pressure is on ticket size.
Expleo.ai: 15% of revenue is influenced by AI today; 5 of the top 20 accounts have adopted it, with a target of all 20 (management cites 60% of revenue influenced by AI).
Middle East: financial services unaffected and growing, but non-BFSI sectors (e.g. retail in Dubai) faced headwinds from shipping disruption; management expects a recovery from around June.
European automotive faces headwinds in Germany and France per the Chairman; Europe remains the fastest-growing region.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth and EBITDA margin should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO guided to sustainable double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA held at current levels, reiterating the 15% to 16% range (without other income) as a range he is confident in.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA flat YoY despite currency tailwinds, and can margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited wage revisions of 8% to 10% in the market and Labor Code costs, offset by opex controls; forex benefit is partly negated by on-site costs in Belgium, Dubai and the US.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AI productivity gain is passed back to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said most of the savings go back to customers, with premium pricing on AI services not offsetting it; some multi-year fixed-bid contracts may allow clawback, but pricing is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What are the loans of INR 100 crore, and why no dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said loans are to the Expleo Group as related-party transactions at about 9.5% to 10%. Chairman said dividend is deferred as the priority is M&A execution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for aerospace and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the outlook is positive, with Boeing, Airbus and Dassault wanting India manufacturing, but government-to-government timing is unpredictable; no forward percentage was given. Offset obligations from Indo-French deals were pushed to late FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East and geopolitical impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said financial services is unaffected and growing, while retail and non-BFSI sectors are hit; Israel demand is rising and Saudi defence testing opportunities are being pursued without deals signed yet.

risks_watch: Constant-currency revenue growth was only 0.7% YoY in Q4 and -0.4% for FY26, so reported growth depends on currency.
AI-driven ticket size compression and pass-through of productivity gains to clients could pressure revenue per engagement.
Adjusted EBITDA margin fell QoQ to 15.5% from 16.6%, with wage inflation of 8% to 10% and Labor Code costs.
Group revenue dependence: around 30% to 33% of revenue from Expleo Group.
Geopolitical exposure in Middle East and Israel; European automotive headwinds; defence timing dependent on government-to-government deals.
Watch whether the first M&A deal closes next quarter, and the dividend decision after M&A.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the financial results, with a clear focus on AI-led growth and margin protection. More cautious and evasive on specifics: no Egypt revenue number, no aerospace-defence percentage target, and no FY27 numeric revenue guidance beyond double digits.
key_quotes: This is not a favor anymore. This is a demand.
So, the only way we want to overcome this is by increasing the volume rather than going after big ticket items, which may not be the way to go in future.
We're very happy to announce that 70% of our organization is now AI qualified.
So, the win rate has not been challenged, but the ticket size and the ability to draw the same revenue of last year is what will be under pressure.
